topic: Why we stopped running a weekly all-hands and what replaced it
audience: Heads of operations and founders at companies of 30 to 150 people
author: Dario Venn, COO at Lanternworks (fictional)

material.figure: The Monday all-hands cost 62 person-hours a week across 62 people
material.dated_event: On 9 June we cancelled it with two days' notice and no replacement ready
material.changed_belief: I believed a weekly all-hands was the cheapest way to keep everyone aligned
material.before_after: Questions asked in the open went from about 3 a week in the meeting to 19 a week in the written thread within a month
material.quote: Ines in finance wrote: 'I have never once asked a question in that meeting and I have asked four this week.'
steps: Each team lead posts a written update by Monday 10:00
Questions go in one thread, answered by Wednesday
A 20-minute call on the first Monday of the month, questions only

must_include: the two weeks where it went badly
